concepts.why: The presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial lung disease, and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The combination of symmetric joint swelling, ulcers, elevated ferritin, and characteristic skin biopsy findings are consistent with this diagnosis.

The presence of immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies, interstitial lung disease, and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The combination of symmetric joint swelling, elevated ferritin, and characteristic skin biopsy findings are consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT support this diagnosis.
The presence of ulcers and characteristic skin biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
The combination of elevated ferritin and lymphocytopenia are consistent with this diagnosis.
The presence of hilar lymphadenopathy and interstitial lung disease support this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Fatigue is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in many conditions.
rationales.F04: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal joints is a characteristic feature of rheumatologic diseases.
rationales.F05: Dorsal MCP ulcers are a characteristic feature of dermatomyositis and other rheumatologic diseases.
rationales.F08: Anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies are a specific marker for Sjögren's Syndrome and can also be seen in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
rationales.F09: Hilar lymphadenopathy and interstitial lung disease can be seen in various rheumatologic and pulmonary conditions.
rationales.F10: Worsening interstitial lung disease is a characteristic feature of progressive pulmonary conditions.
rationales.F11: Restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity is a characteristic feature of interstitial lung disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including symmetric joint swelling, ulcers, and interstitial lung disease, along with positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and elevated ferritin, are most consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, which explains the combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis.
